about.title: Carlsbad Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A product that fails in Carlsbad can be almost anything: a power tool bought for a home project, a car part that gives out on I-5 or Palomar Airport Road, a space heater, a child's car seat, a medication with a warning label that left something out. When that failure hurts someone, California treats it differently from an ordinary accident. Product liability cases here often rest on strict liability. That means you generally need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how it was made, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. Whether the manufacturer was careless is usually beside the point. Responsibility can also reach beyond the factory. The distributor and the store that sold the item in San Diego County may share in it. LawProactive is not a law firm. We connect Carlsbad residents, at no cost, with an independent attorney who handles these claims on contingency, so you can find out where you stand without spending anything up front.

whyChoose.title: Why Carlsbad Residents Use LawProactive for Product Cases

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In many California product cases you do not have to prove the company was negligent, only that the product was defective and that defect caused your injury. An attorney who knows this framework can focus your claim where it belongs.

items.title: The product is the evidence
items.desc: Keeping the item itself — along with packaging, receipts, and instructions — is often the single most important step. A network attorney can tell you how to preserve it and arrange proper inspection before anyone throws it out or sends it back.

items.title: More than one party may answer for it
items.desc: The manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer that sold the product in San Diego County can each be liable under California law. Identifying every responsible link in that chain is part of what the attorney we connect you with will look at.

items.question: My tire failed on I-5 near Carlsbad and I crashed. Is that a car accident case or a product case?
items.answer: It can be both. Carlsbad recorded 499 injury collisions in 2025 with 682 people hurt, and a portion of crashes anywhere involve equipment that did not perform as it should. If a defective tire, brake system, or airbag played a role, a strict liability claim against the maker or seller may exist alongside any claim involving another driver. Keep the vehicle and the failed part exactly as they are until an attorney has looked at them.

items.question: I already threw away the broken product. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Possibly, though it is harder. Photos, the receipt, the model and serial number, the packaging, medical records describing how you were hurt, and any similar items you still own can help reconstruct what happened. Tell the attorney you connect with exactly what you have, and do not dispose of anything else related to the incident.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free connection service, not a law firm, and we do not charge you at any point. The independent attorneys in our network handle product liability claims on contingency, which means there is no attorney fee unless they recover compensation for you.
